question: Which phylum of the animal kingdom is made up of segmented insects like earthworms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Annelida**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Annelida** is the phylum that includes segmented worms such as earthworms.
 
• Members of the phylum **Annelida** have bodies that are divided into segments.
 
• This phylum is distinct from **Porifera** (sponges), **Nematoda** (roundworms), and **Platyhelminthes** (flatworms).
 
• Annelids exhibit a high degree of specialization in their segmented body structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **phylum Annelida** includes other organisms like leeches and polychaetes in addition to earthworms.
 
• Earthworms play a crucial role in soil health by aerating the soil and breaking down organic matter.
 
• Annelids have a coelom, which is a fluid-filled cavity that houses their internal organs and allows for greater flexibility and mobility.
 
• They have a closed circulatory system, meaning their blood is contained within vessels.
 
• The segmentation of annelids allows for more efficient and flexible movement.
